__how_to_use_this_template: This template documents every WorldSpec field in the order the pipeline applies them.
Keys starting with '__' are documentation only and are silently dropped at parse time.
Fill in the 8 STEPS below in order. Each step lists what is known so far and what to decide.
Don't include fields you didn't set — every non-doc key here has a sensible default.
When in doubt, copy a bundled spec (e.g. rolling_plains_river.json) and tweak.
__pipeline_order: 1. Base noise field is sampled in [0,1].  -> set EITHER elevation_profile OR noise_layers.
2. elevation_range linearly remaps that field: e' = clamp01(e * (hi - lo) + lo).
3. The per-spec elevation CDF histogram-normalises e' back into a UNIFORM [0,1] distribution.
After this step, the value q literally means 'q of the terrain area is at or below here'.
This is why sea_level and biome_zones can be specified as TERRAIN FRACTIONS, not noise.
4. spatial_features are applied IN ARRAY ORDER on the post-CDF elevation field.
5. biome_zones are scanned ascending; the first band whose elev_max >= e wins.
6. Rivers are overlaid last: cells whose channel core fires become river_biome.
__y_coordinate_mapping: After the CDF step, elev=sea_level is anchored to Minecraft Y=63 (the water plane).
metres_range = [metresLo, metresHi] sets the full vertical span across elev in [0,1].
Vertical scale is FIXED at 5 metres per block (does NOT change with horizontal world scale).
Peaks above Y=250 are smoothly compressed so they never flatten on the build limit.
Ocean depth uses sqrt compression so deep ocean stays in-bounds.
alpine / mountains: [-300, 800]   -> ~220 blocks of relief (use scale >= 2)
name: Template World
__name_doc: STEP 1 — A short, evocative name for the world. Required.
description: One-line summary of the vibe (used only as metadata).
__description_doc: STEP 1 — Optional one-line summary describing the feel of the world.
__seed_offset_doc: STEP 1 — Integer XOR'd into the world seed. Use a distinct number per spec if you ship many specs so they don't share rng artefacts when generated under the same world seed.
__STEP_2_choose_base_noise: Pick ONE of {elevation_profile, noise_layers}. Use elevation_profile for a single coherent terrain texture; use noise_layers when you want to blend two distinct styles (e.g. broad rolling base + sparse ridged mountains).

elevation_profile.__doc: STEP 2 (single-layer option). All seven modes are listed below; pick one and delete the others mentally — only the fields relevant to your chosen mode are read.

__mode_doc.fbm: rolling/organic — default; best for plains, taigas, forests, deserts
__mode_doc.billow: puffy bumps (|fbm|-shaped) — soft hills, dunes, ice domes
__mode_doc.ridged: sharp positive ridges — mountain crests, alpine spines
__mode_doc.domain_warp: fbm with swirled coords — organic islands, marbled coasts, swamps
__mode_doc.domain_warp_ridged: swirled ridges — twisted mountain chains, volcanic spines
__mode_doc.cellular: voronoi cells — basalt columns, mosaic biomes, faceted archipelagos
__mode_doc.stepped: fbm quantised into N plateaus + jitter — savanna terraces (or use mesa_step feature instead)

elevation_profile.__frequency_doc: Noise cells per tile (1 tile = 1024 blocks horizontally at scale 1). 1.5–3 = continent-sized features; 3–6 = sub-continental variety (most worlds); 6–12 = busier; >15 starts to look noisy and repetitive.
elevation_profile.__octaves_doc: Integer 1..10. Each extra octave adds finer detail at higher frequency. 4–7 is typical. 8+ is very rugged. (Only the first octave defines the broad shape.)
elevation_profile.__persistence_doc: 0..1. How much each finer octave contributes. 0.3 = soft and smooth; 0.5 = balanced; 0.7 = jagged and chaotic.
elevation_profile.__lacunarity_doc: Frequency multiplier between octaves. 2.0 standard. <2 = octaves overlap (less detail spread); >2 = each octave is much finer than the last.
elevation_profile.__sharpness_doc: ridged / domain_warp_ridged only. 1 = rounded; 2–3 = sharp ridges; 4+ = knife-edge crests.
elevation_profile.__warp_strength_doc: domain_warp / domain_warp_ridged only. 0 = identical to fbm; 0.4–0.6 = pleasant organic swirl; 1.0+ = trippy curls.
elevation_profile.__stepped_doc: stepped mode only. n_steps = number of terrace levels (3–8 typical); jitter = small noise so terraces aren't perfectly flat (0.01–0.05).
elevation_profile.__cellular_doc: cellular mode only. cell_mode = {f1, f1_inv, f2_minus_f1}. f1 = distance to nearest seed (blobs); f1_inv = 1 - f1 (sharp peaked cells); f2_minus_f1 = veined cell boundaries (best for archipelago coastlines). cell_jitter 0..1 randomises seed positions inside cells (1.0 = full random).

noise_layers.__doc: STEP 2 (multi-layer option). DELETE elevation_profile if you use noise_layers. Each entry has all elevation_profile fields plus 'weight', 'blend', and optional 'mask'.

noise_layers.__example_doc: Sparse ridged crests added on top of the rolling base, gated by a low-frequency mask so they only appear in some regions.

mask.__mask_doc: A separate low-frequency fbm gate in [0,1]. Layer contributes fully where mask > threshold + softness, blends to 0 below threshold - softness. invert flips that.

__noise_layers_blend_doc: 'average' (default) = weighted mean across average-blend layers; 'add' = appended ON TOP after the average. Mix one base 'average' layer with one or two 'add' layers to layer features on top.
__elevation_range_doc: STEP 3 — Linear remap of raw noise BEFORE CDF normalisation. Constraint: 0 <= lo < hi <= 1. Default [0, 1] is correct for almost every world. Tightening (e.g. [0.3, 0.8]) shrinks the input distribution so the CDF step does less stretching, which can make rivers/coastlines feel less varied. Leave at [0, 1] unless you have a specific reason.
__sea_level_doc: STEP 4 — TERRAIN FRACTION in [0,1] AFTER CDF normalisation. sea_level=0.30 means roughly the lowest 30% of land becomes underwater. Guidance: mostly-land world 0.05–0.20; balanced 0.25–0.40; ocean world 0.55–0.80. Rivers carve their channels to (sea_level - 0.035) so they fill with water.
__metres_range_doc: STEP 4 — Real-world metres across elev=0 (deepest ocean floor) to elev=1 (highest peak). Final Y is anchored at sea_level=63 and capped at Y=250 (smoothly compressed). See __y_coordinate_mapping above for recommendations by world type.

spatial_features.__doc: STEP 5 — Optional ordered pipeline of post-CDF transforms. Each entry mutates the [0,1] elevation field, then the next entry sees the mutated field.
spatial_features.__type_doc_river: Adds a stateless analytic river network: meandering channels that carve to (sea_level - 0.035) ONLY where terrain is in the lower half of its band. Rivers naturally avoid mountains.

__river_param_doc.river_freq: Tile-unit frequency of the meander network. 0.3 = sparse mighty rivers; 0.55 = a handful; 0.9 = dense network. (1 tile = 1024 blocks at scale 1.)
__river_param_doc.river_warp: 0..1 meander wiggliness via domain warp. 0.5 typical.
__river_param_doc.river_octaves: Octaves of the warp field. 3–5 typical.
__river_param_doc.river_width: Channel half-width in TILE units (0.0024 ≈ 2–3 blocks at scale 1). Constant width regardless of terrain steepness.
__river_param_doc.bank_width: Ramp width from channel edge to bank top (tile units).
__river_param_doc.tributary_strength: 0 = clean main channels only; 1 = full secondary network of smaller rivers. Mangrove deltas raise this.

spatial_features.__type_doc_sea_threshold: Adds a constant offset to elevation. NEGATIVE pushes terrain down (more ocean / sinks land). POSITIVE lifts. Use AFTER you've picked your base noise to nudge the overall land/sea ratio without redoing the CDF math.
spatial_features.__hint: Note: the CDF was already built — sea_threshold operates POST-normalisation so it's just a vertical shift on the final field. Smaller numbers (|offset| <= 0.2) feel natural.

spatial_features.__type_doc_stretch: Linear remap of the current [0,1] field to [to[0], to[1]]. Use to flatten the world (e.g. to=[0.3, 0.7] compresses everything toward the middle) or to push extremes (to=[0.0, 1.2] then clamps). Seamless across tiles.

spatial_features.__type_doc_coastal_smooth: Pulls elevation NEAR sea_level toward sea_level itself — widens beaches, softens coasts, creates flat marshlands. width = neighbourhood around sea_level; strength = pull magnitude (0..1). Pass null for sea_level to use the top-level spec.sea_level.

spatial_features.__type_doc_mesa_step: Quantises elevation into n_steps terraces (with light jitter so each step isn't a perfect plane). Classic badlands look. Apply BEFORE river to let rivers carve through the steps; apply AFTER river to step the carved valleys.

spatial_features.__type_doc_dune_ridges: Parallel sinusoidal dunes, modulated by a slow mask so they appear in patches. direction_deg in degrees (0 = east, 90 = north); spacing = dune period in tile units; amplitude = elevation displacement.

__feature_order_recipes.alpine_with_valley_rivers: [river]                                                       — rivers form only in lowlands, mountains untouched
__feature_order_recipes.carved_mesa_with_river: [mesa_step, river]                                            — terraces first, river carves through them
__feature_order_recipes.mangrove_delta: [river (high tributary_strength), coastal_smooth]             — dense branching channels + marsh coasts
__feature_order_recipes.drowned_continent: [sea_threshold(-0.4), coastal_smooth]                         — most land sinks, remaining coasts are gentle
__feature_order_recipes.stepped_island_chain: [stretch([0,1]), mesa_step, coastal_smooth]                   — discrete elevation tiers ringed by beaches
__feature_order_recipes.twisted_volcanic_islands: [coastal_smooth]   (pair with domain_warp_ridged base noise)  — cone peaks rising from warm sea

__biome_zones_doc: STEP 6 — List of (elev_max, biome) bands sorted ascending by elev_max. The first band whose elev_max >= cell's elev wins.
- The LAST entry MUST have elev_max: 1.0 (otherwise validation fails).
- Bands must be sorted ascending and have unique elev_max.
- Each biome name must appear in __valid_biomes below (BiomeRegistry).
TIP: choose your thresholds so sea_level is INSIDE one of them — ocean biomes below sea_level, beach biomes immediately above, then your land biomes.
TIP: for a 'mostly one biome' world, give that biome the widest band (e.g. plains 0.20–0.85).
__river_biome_doc: STEP 7 — Biome painted on cells where a river channel fired (only used when a 'river' spatial_feature is present). Common picks: 'river' for temperate worlds, 'frozen_river' for snow/tundra worlds.
__how_to_think_about_a_new_world: 1. Pick the dominant vibe and the climate (warm/cold, wet/dry).
2. Pick a base noise mode that matches the SHAPE you want:
3. Decide how much OCEAN (sea_level fraction) and how much VERTICAL RELIEF (metres_range).
4. Lay out biome_zones from low (ocean) to high (peaks) so the last band is at 1.0.
5. Add spatial_features for character (river for waterways, mesa_step for terraces, dunes, etc.).
6. Set river_biome to match climate (frozen_river for cold worlds).
7. Pick a seed_offset distinct from other shipped specs.
